verdict.rationale: Moneybird's own docs say a personal API token can be scoped via checkboxes, and OAuth tokens can be revoked through an RFC 7009 endpoint, so an agent can be given a scoped credential that can be ended. However, the docs warn that personal tokens come 'at a cost of security,' and the evidence never shows how fine-grained the scopes are or any agent-specific least-privilege controls. missing for 10: the list and granularity of available scopes, read-only versus write separation, per-administration restriction, token expiry or rotation for personal tokens, agent-specific credential guidance, and independent or hands-on corroboration.

support.subject: As an AI-native user, I can issue scoped/least-privilege API credentials for an agent

citations.quote: For a personal API token, you can use the checkboxes to select the scopes you need.
Alternatively, you can create a personal API token that simplifies the setup, at a cost of security.
Moneybird supports the [OAuth 2.0 Token Revocation](https://datatracker.ietf.org/doc/html/rfc7009) endpoint at `https://moneybird.com/oauth/revoke`.
